name: CA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+19
Garamendi's incumbency and large financial advantage
Challenger raised only about $20,000 with $235 on hand
Prediction markets price Garamendi near 96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Garamendi: a D+19 district, incumbency, and a massive money edge against a challenger with essentially no campaign treasury. Markets agree, pricing him around 96%, so the race stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Garamendi or a surge of Republican-leaning national environment would be needed to make this competitive, and neither is evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
John Garamendi, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Northern California district that leans about 19 points Democratic. He has raised roughly $489,000 and holds more than $1.1 million in cash, while Republican Rudy Recile has raised about $20,000 and reports just $235 on hand, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and markets. Prediction markets give Garamendi about a 96 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided fundraising gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with only a remote chance of an upset.
